items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: And, well, during that two years I was with Al Hurd, we went up there, they flew us up there to do the Mardi Gras ball

ctx.x: Yeah, Al, every year they usually select a New Orleans band.

And I don't know what's going on in the last few years, but in the days of Al Hurd, when I was with Al Hurd, rather, around that era of time that we were getting a band from New Orleans, I think Senator Long was always in charge, I think, of, I had a lot to do with anyway, the annual Mardi Gras ball, which is usually held in the Mayflower every year. And, well, during that two years I was with Al Hurd, we went up there, they flew us up there to do the Mardi Gras ball, put us up in the Mayflower overnight, and it…
Is that the same as here? I mean, do they have a tableau or call outs?

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: Until 56 when Al Hurts says, Bob, why don't you quit your day job and come work with me?

ctx.x: How did you get interested in bass by the way?

Well I always did like bass. I always did like string bass, Dick. And around 1937 after playing the guitar for four years in the band I decided, well you know the bass player with the Al Streaming Band who was the vice president of the Soil Company and had to do all that road traveling. He was told Streaming and he said, Al I'm going to have to quit the band. He said, I got too much traveling. He had been with the band ten years. So he left the band and that's when Al told me, he said, Bob why don't you switch…
But why does Treeman want you on bass? Do you know?
